content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] streaming.p99 > 10s across us-west-2. Multiple routes reporting tail stalls & increased prefill decode time. SLO breach detected (p95/p99). Severity: P2. auto-created incident #INC-2026-145.
oncall-alex: on it. grabbing logs and checking recent deploys.
sre-leah: thx. any customer impact reports yet?
customer-support-chi: a few customers in west reported timeouts/non-responses ~10:10-10:18. support ticket IDs: SUP-4921, SUP-4923. They see streaming stalls and incomplete chunks.
infra-marc: infra metrics show KV cache evictions spike at 10:08 UTC; slab reuse dropped to 42%. Eviction rate: 840/s on 3 shards.
runtime-anya: that matches increased prefill hit ratio drop. We're seeing prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill threads backing up while decode workers idle. likely fragmentation -> tiny free slabs -> more eviction churn.
oncall-alex: quick mitigation ideas: 1) throttle prefill to reduce eviction pressure, 2) temporarily disable prefill on noisy routes, 3) increase cache slab allocation to streaming cluster. which is lowest risk?
sre-leah: throttle prefill first. push small config change to reduce prefill concurrency by 50% for streaming routes. if no improvement, disable prefill for top noisy prefix.
eng-ops-ryan: can we route streaming requests to fallback model variant with smaller kv footprint? that buys time but might affect quality.
runtime-anya: yes we have model-lite-1 compatible. can route by policy to lite variant in us-west-2. need to update routing config and trigger immediate reload.
incident-bot: @oncall-alex check-in timer started (15m).
oncall-alex: applying prefill throttle now. patch:```
PATCH /configs/prefill
{
  "routes": ["/v1/stream/*"],
  "prefill_concurrency_pct": 50
}
```
infra-marc: I see the config hit the edge. KV eviction rate dropped to 320/s within 40s. slab reuse up to 61%.
customer-support-chi: customers SUP-4921 and SUP-4923 confirm improvement on their next requests. still occasional stalls for long sequences.
sre-leah: that's promising. look at p95/p99 graphs.
runtime-anya: p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 1.4s, p99 from 11.2s -> 3.9s. streaming tail stalls reduced but not eliminated. still some nodes show prefill latency spikes ~600-800ms.
oncall-alex: load distribution across shards?
infra-marc: yes, shard-7 and shard-11 still hot. fragmentation hotspots: slab free fragments many small holes. Paging counts high for those shards.
sre-leah: recommend coordinated follow-ups: 1) schedule slab defrag on shard-7/11, 2) apply eviction-imbalance patch to prefer keeping long-lived entries (increase LRU bias), 3) consider temporary routing of 5% traffic to model-lite.
eng-ops-ryan: I can flip 5% routing to model-lite-1 now for us-west-2 streaming. doing canary.
runtime-anya: canary applied. monitor quality metrics and token-level errors.
incident-bot: @oncall-alex update requested: current SLO status: p95 within SLO, p99 still above target but trending down. customer impact: reduced, a few high-volume customers still affected.
oncall-alex: accepted. starting slab defrag on shard-7 (non-disruptive background job) and apply LRU-bias patch.
infra-marc: defrag job started:```
# run defrag on shard-7
curl -X POST https://infra.internal/api/kv/defrag -d '{"shard":"7","mode":"background"}'
```
sre-leah: note: defrag is I/O heavy. keeping off-peak limits. watching streaming latencies.
customer-support-chi: one high-traffic customer (ENT-334) reported degraded throughput earlier. they're now reporting improvement after throttle & canary.
runtime-anya: after LRU-bias patch, eviction churn fell further. prefill hit ratio recovering to 78%.
oncall-alex: good. next steps: 1) keep prefill throttle for 2 hours, 2) keep 5% model-lite canary for 30 minutes, 3) monitor p99 and paging metrics, 4) open follow-up to improve allocator to avoid tiny-fragmentation (ENG-ALLOC-89).
eng-ops-ryan: opening ENG ticket and PR for routing automation to fall back to lite variants automatically on eviction surge.
incident-bot: incident #INC-2026-145 updated: mitigation in place, severity downgraded to P3, postmortem required.
sre-leah: ack. I'll own the postmortem, include timeline, metrics, customer impact, and long-term mitigations (allocator changes, smarter prefill heuristics).
oncall-alex: thanks everyone. any outstanding actions?
runtime-anya: follow-up: capture KV heap histograms across shards (for PM). I'll collect and attach to the incident.
infra-marc: I'll schedule a maintenance window to run deep defrag on affected shards during off-peak tonight.
customer-support-chi: I'll batch customer updates and add ETA for full recovery.
oncall-alex: closing handoff to SRE for root-cause & postmortem. tagging @sre-leah as incident owner.
incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 10:24 UTC. postmortem due in 72h.
